# Release workflow for Zenece

## Scope

Use this skill when changing release behavior, preparing a release, branching from `main`, or updating the project’s Git conventions described in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) and [scripts/start-task.sh](../../../scripts/start-task.sh).

## Required conventions

- Start from an up-to-date `main` branch before beginning work.
- Use the task branch helper script with one of the allowed categories: `feature`, `templating`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, or `refactor`.
- Keep commit messages in Conventional Commits format.
- Do not change the release flow unless the task explicitly requires it.
- Honor the project’s lightweight workflow: do not introduce complex CI or release tooling beyond the existing scripts.

## Working rules

- Use the helper script to create feature branches consistently:
  - `./scripts/start-task.sh feature investor-dashboard`
  - `./scripts/start-task.sh templating refresh-hero`
  - `./scripts/start-task.sh fix mobile-overflow`
- Keep branch names aligned with the pattern `type/slug` generated by the script.
- Use commit types such as `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, or `refactor` when making changes.
- Validate release-related changes by reading the current scripts and ensuring they still match the documented workflow.

## Anti-patterns to avoid

- Do not work from a non-`main` branch without using the helper script.
- Do not invent a different release process or versioning strategy.
- Do not widen the release workflow beyond the repo’s existing simple SemVer script.

## Good examples in this repo

- [scripts/start-task.sh](../../../scripts/start-task.sh) enforces `main`-based task creation and type/slug naming.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) documents the release flow and Conventional Commits rules.
- [scripts/release.sh](../../../scripts/release.sh) handles SemVer bumping, annotated tagging, and release updates in a minimal way.
